====Noun====
[[Image:Stilles Mineralwasser.jpg|thumb|water (1,2)]]
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q283}}{{lb|en|uncountable}} A inorganic compound (of molecular formula H<sub>2</sub>O) found at [[room temperature]] and pressure as a clear [[liquid]]; it is present naturally as [[rain#Noun|rain]], and found in [[river]]s, [[lake]]s and [[sea]]s; its solid form is [[ice#Noun|ice]] and its gaseous form is [[steam#Noun|steam]].
#: {{ux|en|By the action of electricity, the '''water''' was resolved into its two parts, oxygen and hydrogen.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1805|month=December|author=Julius Griffiths|title=A Journey across the Desert|journal=The Monthly Mirror|page=362
|passage=It is wholly out of the power of language to convey any idea of the blissful enjoyment of obtaining '''water''', after an almost total want of it, during eight and forty hours, in the scorching regions of an Arabian desert, in the month of July.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katie-l-burke Katie L. Burke]| magazine=w:American Scientist| title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/in-the-news-47 In the News]| passage=Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis: the ability to convert '''water''' and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and waste oxygen using solar energy.}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable|in particular}} The liquid form of this substance: liquid H<sub>2</sub>O.
##: {{ux|en|May I have a glass of '''water'''?}}
##: {{ux|en|Your plants need more '''water'''.}}
##* {{quote-text|en|year=1835|author=Sir {{w|John Ross (Arctic explorer)|John Ross}}; Sir {{w|James Clark Ross}}|title=[http://books.google.com.au/books?id=SdQBAAAAYAAJ Narrative of a Second Voyage in Search of a North-west Passage &hellip;, Volume 1]|pages=284–5
|passage=Towards the following morning, the thermometer fell to 5°; and at daylight, there was not an atom of '''water''' to be seen in any direction.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Arthur T. Hubbard|title=Encyclopedia of Surface and Colloid Science|isbn=0824707966|page=4895
|passage=A '''water''' drop placed on the surface of ice can either spread or form a lens depending on the properties of the three phases involved in wetting, i.e., on the properties of the ice, '''water''', and gas phases.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-05-11|volume=407|issue=8835|page=80|magazine=w:The Economist| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21577341-worlds-third-largest-area-ice-about-undergo-systematic The climate of Tibet: Pole-land]| passage=Of all the transitions brought about on the Earth’s surface by temperature change, the melting of ice into '''water''' is the starkest. It is binary. And for the land beneath, the air above and the life around, it changes everything.}}
##* {{see more citations|en}}
## {{lb|en|countable}} A [[serving#Noun|serving]] of liquid water.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Lori Foster; Erin McCarthy; Amy Garvey| title=Bad Boys of Summer| isbn=0758209347| page=91| passage=Joe bustled back and offered her a glass of wine but she shook her head. “Just a '''water''', please.”}}
# {{lb|en|alchemy|philosophy}} The aforementioned liquid, considered one of [[w:Classical_element|the Classical elements]] or basic elements of alchemy.
#: {{ux|en|He showed me the river of living '''water''', sparkling like crystal, flowing from the throne of God.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|or|in the plural}} Water in a body; an area of [[open#Adjective|open]] water.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Love's Labour's Lost|V|i|138|2|''Roſa.'' O vain peticioner, beg a greater matter,<br>Thou now requeſts but Mooneſhine in the '''water'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage='Twas early June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the '''water''' of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.}}
#* '''2019''', [https://web.archive.org/web/20190311070055/https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/south-korea-proposes-rain-project-with-china-to-cut-pollution/4819207.html VOA Learning English] (public domain)
#*: The president expressed hope that creating rain over '''waters''' between the countries would help reduce pollution.
#: {{ux|en|And God said, Let the '''waters''' under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.}}
#: {{ux|en|The boat was found within the territorial '''waters'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|These seals are a common sight in the coastal '''waters''' of Chile.}}
# {{lb|en|poetic|archaic|or|dialectal}} A body of water, almost always a river, sometimes a lake or [[reservoir]], especially in the names given to such bodies.
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Acts|8|36|clxvi|And as they went on their waye <br> they cam vnto a certayne '''water''' <br> and the gelded man ſayde: Se here is water <br> what ſhall lett me to be baptiſed?}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson Poems 1842|II|Morte d’Arthur|4|On one side lay the Ocean, and on one<br>Lay a great '''water''', and the moon was full.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|editor=William Allingham|year=1865| title=The Ballad Book: a selection of the choicest British ballads| section=William and May Margaret, or the Water of Clyde|passage=But ere he came to Clyde's '''water,''' fu' loud the wind did blaw.}}
# A combination of water and other substance(s).
## {{lb|en|sometimes|countable}} Mineral water.
##: {{ux|en|Perrier is the most popular '''water''' in this restaurant.}}
## {{lb|en|countable|often|in the plural}} [[spa|Spa]] water.
##: {{ux|en|Many people visit Bath to take the '''waters'''.}}
## {{lb|en|pharmacy}} A [[solution]] in water of a [[gaseous]] or readily [[volatile]] [[substance]].
##: {{ux|en|ammonia '''water'''}}
## [[urine|Urine]]. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=w:George R.R. Martin| title=A Clash of Kings| publisher=Bantam| year_published=2011| page=458| passage=Ser Dunaver's squire Jodge could not hold his '''water''' when he slept.}}
## {{senseid|en|amniotic fluid}} [[amniotic fluid|Amniotic fluid]] or the [[amniotic sac]] containing it. {{qual|Used only in the plural in the UK but often also in the singular in North America.}}
##: {{syn|en|bag of waters}}
##: {{ux|en|Before the child is born, the pregnant woman’s '''water''' breaks. {{qualifier|North America}}}}
##: {{ux|en|Before your child is born, your '''water(s)''' will break. {{qualifier|North America}}}}
##: {{ux|en|Before the child is born, the pregnant woman’s '''waters''' break. {{qualifier|UK}}}}
## {{lb|en|colloquial|medicine}} Fluids in the body, especially when causing [[swelling]].
##: {{ux|en|He suffers from '''water''' on the knee.}}
# {{lb|en|business|often|attributive}} The water [[supply#Noun|supply]], as a [[service]] or [[utility]].
#: {{cot|en|electricity|internet|phone#Noun|power#Noun|sewer}}
#: {{ux|en|The city threatened to cut off our '''water''' after we went only a month without paying our bill.}}
#: {{ux|en|Did you leave the '''water''' running again?}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|in the plural|or|in the singular}} A state of affairs; [[condition#Noun|condition]]s; usually with an [[adjective]] indicating an [[adverse]] condition.
#: {{ux|en|The rough '''waters''' of change will bring about the calm after the storm.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial|figuratively}} A person's [[intuition]]. <!--is this always in the plural?-->
#: {{syn|en|bones}}
#: {{ux|en|I know he'll succeed. I feel it in my '''waters'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|dated|finance}} Excess [[valuation]] of [[securities]].
#* {{quote-journal|en| title=Too Much '''Water''' to Suit Cummins| passage=Iowa Governor Will Fight Rock Island Reorganization. He Says That Under the New Plan Too Much '''Water''' Is Put Into the Stock&mdash;Believes Plan Is Out of Harmony with Iowa Laws.| work=The Atlanta Constitution| date=August 2, 1902}}
#* {{quote-journal|en| title=Says Stock ''''Water'''' Didn't Affect Fare| work=New York Times| date=April 11, 1920| passage=the outstanding stock and bond obligations of the company were reduced from $34,000,000 to $24,000,000 by squeezing out the '''water'''.}}
# A particular [[quality]] or [[appearance]] suggestive of water:
## The [[limpidity]] and [[lustre]] of a precious stone, especially a [[diamond]].
##: {{ux|en|a diamond of the first '''water''' is perfectly pure and transparent}}
##* {{RQ:Woolf Orlando|passage=And when she raised it to see what caused this agitation, she saw nothing—nothing but the vast solitary emerald which Queen Elizabeth had given her. And was that not enough? she asked. It was of the finest '''water'''.}}
## A [[wavy]], [[lustrous]] pattern or decoration such as is imparted to [[linen]], [[silk]], [[metal]]s, etc.

=====Translations=====
{{see translation subpage|Noun}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|wateren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wæterian}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*watrōną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*watrijaną}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*watōr|t=water}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wódr̥|t=water}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|watter||water}}, {{cog|stq|woaterje|t=to water}}, {{cog|fy|wetterje|t=to water}}, {{cog|nl|wateren|t=to water}}, {{cog|nds-de|watern|t=to water}}, {{cog|de|wässern|t=to water}}, {{cog|da|vande|t=to water}}, {{cog|sv|vattna|t=to water}}, {{cog|is|vatna|t=to water}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}
[[Image:To water the coffee tree in dry season.jpg|thumb|right|to water (1)]]

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To pour water into the [[soil#Noun|soil]] surrounding (plants).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1900|author=L. Frank Baum|title=The Wonderful Wizard of Oz|chapter=24|passage=Aunt Em had just come out of the house to '''water''' the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[wet#Verb|wet]] or supply with water; to [[moisten]]; to overflow with water; to [[irrigate]].
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=9|passage=tears '''watering''' the ground|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Longfellow Evangeline|I
|passage=Men whose lives glided on like rivers that '''water''' the woodlands.}}
# {{senseid|en|to provide with water}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide (animals) with water for [[drink#Verb|drink]]ing.
#: {{ux|en|I need to '''water''' the cattle.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008| title=Mopus|author=Oisin Curran | page=34| passage=While they '''watered''' and washed their horses, I talked with a red-capped man, some kind of chief.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To get or take in water.
#: {{ux|en|The ship put into port to '''water'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1944|month=January and February|author=W. McGowan Gradon|title=Forres as a Railway Centre|journal=Railway Magazine|page=23|text=After working the 1.30 p.m. through train from Forres to Aberdeen as far as Elgin, she returns tender first with a local passenger train and is then coaled and '''watered''' at Forres shed, and eventually works back to Perth on the 10.20 p.m. through freight.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[urinate]] onto.
#: {{syn|en|see [[Thesaurus:urinate]]}}
#: {{ux|en|[[nature calls|Nature called]], so I stepped into the woods and '''watered''' a tree.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[dilute]].
#: {{syn|en|water down}}
#: {{ant|en|refine}} <!--is it really?-->
#: {{ux|en|Can you '''water''' the whisky, please?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|dated|finance}} To overvalue (securities), especially through deceptive accounting.
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=Calls Rail Holding Companies Threat|work=The Sun| date=April 10, 1930| passage=such agencies would make it possible for the railroads to '''water''' stock and evade the law subjecting security issues to public regulation}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To fill with or secrete water or similar liquid.
#: {{ux|en|Chopping onions makes my eyes '''water'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The smell of fried onions makes my mouth '''water'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To wet and [[calender]], as cloth, so as to impart to it a [[lustrous]] appearance in [[wavy]] lines; to [[diversify]] with wavelike lines.
#: {{ux|en|to '''water''' silk}}
